- Implement automated Apex tests with sufficient coverage on all deployment pipelines.
- Use delta deployments to reduce deployment scope and failure surface.
- Review failed deployments for recurring error patterns (missing dependencies, permission issues).

- Break large features into smaller pull requests that are faster to review and merge.
- Set up automated PR validation pipelines to reduce manual review bottlenecks.

Salesforce blocked the email because the sender domain is not verified (Spring '26 Email-Sending Domain Verification, enforced since April 2026).

Fix one of the following:

  1. DKIM key (recommended): Setup > Email > DKIM Keys
     - Generate a key for the sending domain.
     - Publish the CNAME records in DNS.
     - Enable the key.

  2. Authorized Email Domain: Setup > Email > Email Administration > Authorized Email Domains
     - Add the sending domain.
     - Complete the verification flow.

  3. Organization-Wide Email Address: Setup > Email > Organization-Wide Email Addresses
     - Create and verify an address.
     - Grant profile access to the running user.

  4. Sandbox workaround: Setup > Email > Deliverability
     - Enable "Use a substitute email address for unverified domains".
     - From address becomes email@<id>.sfcustomeremail.com (display name and reply-to preserved).
     - Recommended for sandboxes because DKIM keys / Authorized Email Domains are NOT copied on refresh.
     - Does not apply to @gmail.com / @hotmail.com / @outlook.com senders or Free Suite / trial orgs.

See https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005316090 for the full timeline and requirements.
emailErrorAdviceNoMailPermission:
Salesforce blocked the email because the org-wide Email Deliverability access level is too low (typically "System email only", which is the default for sandboxes and scratch orgs).

Fix: Setup > Email > Deliverability
  - Change "Access level" to "All email".
  - Save.

Notes:
  - "System email only" allows only Salesforce-generated alerts (password reset, etc.), not API / Apex-sent emails.
  - The same setting also gates Apex Messaging.sendEmail() and the SOAP sendEmail call used by sfdx-hardis notifications.
  - On sandbox refresh, this setting often resets to "System email only", so this is the most common cause of NO_SINGLE_MAIL_PERMISSION after a refresh.

mfaRecommendationDisableSmsIdentity:
In Setup > Identity Verification:
  - Disable "Let users verify their identity by text message (SMS)".
  - Require a stronger method: Salesforce Authenticator, security key, or built-in authenticator.
mfaRecommendationDisableSmsOnly: In Setup > Identity Verification, disable the option that allows confirming identity by SMS only, so users always need a stronger factor.
mfaRecommendationEnableIdentityConfirmat: In Setup > Session Settings, enable "Require identity verification during multi-factor authentication registration" so a new device registration requires confirming the user's identity first.
mfaRecommendationEnablePhishingResistant: In Setup > Identity Verification, enable "Let users verify their identity with a built-in authenticator" and/or "Let users verify their identity with a security key". Without one of them, privileged users cannot register the method Salesforce requires.
mfaRecommendationEnforceMfaOrgWide:
In Setup > Identity > Identity Verification (or Session Settings):
  - Enable "Require multi-factor authentication for all direct UI logins".
  - Every interactive login then goes through MFA.
mfaRecommendationEnforcePhishingResistan:
The Identity Verification page in Setup is org-wide - there is no per-Profile or per-PermissionSet selector to restrict verification methods to privileged users only.

Two options:

  1. (Recommended) Make sure phishing-resistant methods are available so privileged users CAN register one: Setup > Identity Verification
     - Enable "Let users verify their identity with a built-in authenticator such as Touch ID or Windows Hello".
     - Enable security keys (U2F / WebAuthn) if not already on.
     - Then ask each privileged user to register one now (Salesforce enforcement starts in production orgs on July 20 2026).

  2. (Optional, org-wide impact) On the same page, disable non-phishing-resistant methods for EVERYONE in the org:
     - SMS
     - Email codes
     - Salesforce Authenticator push
     - TOTP apps
     This affects ALL users, not just privileged ones. Many orgs prefer to leave these enabled for non-privileged users and let the Salesforce enforcement auto-block privileged users.

The Salesforce platform enforcement of phishing-resistant MFA (sandboxes since July 10 2026, production starting July 20 2026, staggered by release group) applies only to privileged users; non-privileged users keep their existing methods, but note the separate all-employee MFA enforcement (sandboxes since July 6 2026, production from July 20 2026).
mfaRecommendationGrantLoginHistoryAccess: Grant the running user "View Setup and Configuration" + "Manage Users" so it can read LoginHistory; without that, non-MFA login detection is blind.
mfaRecommendationGrantTwoFactorApi:
Add PermissionsTwoFactorApi (label "Multi-Factor Authentication for API Logins") to a Permission Set assigned to this user (or directly on the user's Profile) so API access is also covered by MFA.

Before enabling, confirm the integration uses one of these OAuth flows:
  - JWT bearer
  - refresh-token
  - client-credentials

The permission BREAKS any integration that still authenticates with username+password:
  - SOAP login()
  - OAuth grant_type=password

Existing access and refresh tokens keep working.
mfaRecommendationGrantVerificationHistor: Grant the running user "View Setup and Configuration" + "Manage Users" so it can read VerificationHistory; without that, phishing-resistant readiness cannot be measured.
mfaRecommendationInvestigateNonMfaLogin: Confirm whether this login was legitimate. If not, suspend the user and force MFA re-registration. If legitimate, harden the session settings so MFA is required for this login flow.
mfaRecommendationRegisterPhishingResista:
Ask this user to register a phishing-resistant MFA method now: Salesforce enforcement is live in sandboxes since July 10 2026 and starts in production orgs on July 20 2026, staggered by release group (see Salesforce Help article 005321563).

Qualifying methods:
  - Security key: FIDO2 / WebAuthn (YubiKey, Google Titan).
  - Built-in authenticator / passkey: Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello, Android passkeys.
  - Cloud-synced passkeys from a FIDO2-compliant password manager (1Password, Bitwarden, iCloud Keychain).

Setup path: Setup > Identity Verification > Identity Verification Methods.

Methods that do NOT qualify: TOTP apps, Salesforce Authenticator push, SMS, email codes.

mfaRecommendationRemoveBypassProfile: Remove PermissionsBypassMFAForUiLogins from the Profile above. Moving the exemption to a tightly-scoped Permission Set is safer than leaving it on a Profile.
